findings.title: Unvalidated next parameter enables external redirect
findings.summary: The next parameter is reflected into a redirect target and can cross to an external validation domain.
findings.evidenceSnippet: Parameter next produced a two-hop chain ending at external-validation.invalid.

findings.title: OAuth callback accepts attacker-controlled redirect URI
findings.summary: Callback handoff allows a caller-controlled destination while forwarding sensitive flow parameters.
findings.evidenceSnippet: redirect_uri, code, and state were reflected into a cross-domain redirect.

findings.title: Fragment token indicator propagated through redirect chain

finding-1.title: Unvalidated next parameter enables external redirect
finding-1.summary: The login endpoint accepts a next parameter and redirects to an external domain without a strict allow-list.

hopSummary: Initial login request reflected next into /redirect.
Second hop crossed from demo.example to external-validation.invalid.

notes: Use only in an authorized validation window.
External destination is a non-collection validation domain.

remediation.summary: Validate redirect destinations server-side before issuing 3xx responses.
recommendations: Use relative paths or a strict allow-list of trusted hosts.
Reject scheme-relative URLs and nested encoded destinations.
Log denied redirect attempts without storing sensitive query values.

finding-2.title: OAuth callback accepts attacker-controlled redirect URI
finding-2.summary: The callback route forwards authorization flow parameters to a caller-controlled redirect_uri.

hopSummary: Callback reflected redirect_uri into Location header.
Flow parameters were preserved across a domain boundary.

notes: Values are redacted in the UI and report.

remediation.summary: Bind callback destinations to registered OAuth client configuration.
recommendations: Ignore redirect_uri values that were not registered for the client.
Use state validation and do not forward authorization codes to untrusted origins.

finding-3.title: Fragment token indicator propagated through redirect chain
finding-3.summary: A URL fragment token indicator remained present after redirecting to a partner domain.

hopSummary: Fragment was present in the analyzed chain.
Final destination was outside the normalized root domain.

notes: Only token indicators are retained in this dataset.

remediation.summary: Strip fragments and sensitive query values before redirects.
recommendations: Normalize outbound URLs and remove fragments before issuing redirects.
